translations.text: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth. Your breasts are lovelier than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume surpasses every spice.
Your name is perfume poured out. That is why the maidens loved you and drew you after you.
Let us run in the fragrance of your perfume. The king brought me into his chamber. Let us rejoice and delight in you. We love your breasts more than wine, and your love is upright.
I am dark and more beautiful than the daughters of Jerusalem, like the shelters of Kedar and the tents of Solomon.
Do not look at me, for I am dark, because the sun has not looked upon me.
My mother's children quarreled with me. They made me keeper of the vineyards, but I did not keep my own vineyard.
Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you graze your flock and where you rest at noon, so that I may not wander among the pastures of your companions.
If you do not know yourself, beautiful among women, go out along the hoofprints of the flock, and graze your young goats in the shepherds' enclosures.
I have compared you, my companion, to my horse and to Pharaoh's chariots.
Your cheeks are very lovely, like a necklace, and your neck like a chain.
They will make you ornaments of gold with studs of silver, until the king reclines there.
The nard gave off its fragrance.
My brother's son is to me a bundle of frankincense resin. He rests between my breasts.
The Son, my brother, is to me a flowering cluster in the vineyard of En Gedi.
Look, you are beautiful, my companion; look, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves' eyes.
Look, you are handsome, my brother's son, lovely within our bed of cypress.
The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters are cypress.
I am a flower of the wilderness, a lily of the valleys.
Like a lily among thorns, so are you, my companion, among the young women.
Like an apple tree among the trees of the wilderness, so is the one I love among the young men. I longed for his shade and sat beneath it, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
Bring me into the wine house. Set love over me.
Strengthen me with perfume; support me with apples, for I am wounded by his love.
His right hand embraces me, and his left hand is beneath my head.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the power and strength of the wilderness: when he rose and raised all the dead, [?] love until he wished.
The voice of my brother's son! Look, he is coming, leaping among the mountains and bounding over the hills.
My brother's son is like a gazelle or a young stag in the mountains of Bethel. Look, he stands behind the wall, looking through the windows and peering through the lattice.
My brother's son speaks and says to me, “Rise and come, my companion, my own beautiful one, my dove.”
For look, winter has passed, and the rain itself has gone away. Flowers have appeared in our land.
The time for pruning has arrived. The voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land. The fig tree has put out its shoots. The vines have blossomed and given off their fragrance.
Arise and come, my beloved, my beautiful lady, my dove, in the shelter of the rock, near [?].
Show me your face and let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.
Catch for us the little foxes that ruin our vineyard. Our vineyard is blossoming.
My brother’s son is mine, and I am his. Who can withstand my brother’s son? For his right arm is raised high.
He pastures among the flowers until the day breathes and the shadows move away.
Return, my brother’s son, and be like a gazelle. Let the daughters of Jerusalem see you. Sit upon Sarel [?] and upon the four [?].

And like a young stag among the rugged mountains. Leap, my brother’s son, like a gazelle. On my bed, during my nights, I seek the one my soul loves. I sought him but did not find him. I called him, but he did not answer me.
I will rise and go around the city, through the marketplaces and the squares. I will seek the one my soul loves. I sought him but did not find him. I called him, but he did not answer me.
The watchmen who guard the city found me. “Have you seen the one my soul loves?”

I had gone only a little beyond them when I found the one my soul loves. I took hold of him and would not let him go until I brought him into my mother’s house, into the inner chambers of the woman who carried me in her womb.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the power and strength of the wilderness: when he rose and raised all the dead, [?] love until he wished.
Who is this woman coming up from the wilderness, like a rising plume of smoke from her incense, like a cloud in the vault of heaven?
Your two breasts flow with milk. Myrrh and frankincense, beyond all the fragrant powder of [?].
Look, Solomon’s bed! Sixty warriors surround it, from among the warriors of Israel.
All of them carry swords and are trained in battle. Each man has his sword at his hip because of the terrors of the night.
King Solomon made himself a carriage from the trees of Lebanon.
He made its pillars of silver. Sardius together with chrysolite; [?] together with [?].

Its support is gold. Its seat is purple. Its clasps and its clasps [?]. Its center is beryl together with jasper, covered in its natural substance. Its interior is paved with sapphire stones. He loved it more than the daughters of Jerusalem.

Go out and look, daughters of Zion, at King Solomon, wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his suffering and on the day of his crucifixion, on the day of his wedding and on the day his heart rejoiced.
Look, you are beautiful, my companion; look, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves. Your hair is like a flock of goats appearing from the mountains of Gilead.
Your teeth are like flocks that have been shorn and have come up from washing. All of them bear twins; they bear seventy-seven, and none of them is barren.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread. Your speech is sweet. Your cheeks are like the rind of a pomegranate, apart from your silence.

Your neck is like the tower of David, built upon Talpioth. A thousand weapons of war hang inside it, where no one sees it and the sun does not reach it, together with all the missiles of the warriors’ house. Three men guard it.
Your two breasts are like two twin fawns of a gazelle grazing among flowers, until the day breathes and the shadows shift.

I myself will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense. The stags of the wilderness anoint themselves with its fragrance, and the birds of the lowlands eat it and do not die, for they renew their youth.
You are altogether beautiful, my companion. You have no blemish; there is none at all upon you.
Come from Lebanon, bride; come from Lebanon. Come and emerge from the beginning of faith, and appear among the mountains of dawn.
From the summit of Senir and Hermon, as you drink the dew, from the dens of lions and from the mountains of leopards.
You have stirred my heart, my sister, my bride. You have stirred my heart at once with your eyes, with a single ornament of your neck.
How lovely your breasts are, my sister, my bride! How much lovelier your breasts are than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than every spice!
Honey drips from your lips. Milk and honey are beneath your tongue, and the scent of your clothes is like the scent of [?].
My sister, my bride, is a locked garden, a locked garden, a sealed spring.
Your shoots are where no craftsman sees them and no thief digs them up: a garden with choice fruit, sandarac with peach trees, henna with nard.
Nard with saffron, fragrant cane and cinnamon, with every frankincense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the finest perfumes.
A garden fountain, a spring of living water flowing from Lebanon.
Rise, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow on my garden, so that my spices may flow. Let my brother’s son come down into his garden and eat its choice fruit.

I have entered my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spices. I have eaten my bread with my honey. I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, my companions, and be satisfied. Drink, sons of my brothers, and become drunk, for they are [?].
Jealousy seizes them, like Selbelianos [?]. A vine became my salvation, cut from Hazazon and planted at Golgotha.
I am asleep, but my heart is awake. The voice of my brother’s son—he is knocking at the door.

“Open to me, my sister, my companion, my dove, my perfect one.” Like a delicate flute and a sweet-sounding lyre, he makes me glad when I hear him. “For my head is covered with dew, and my locks with the moisture of the night.”
I have taken off my garment; how can I put it on? I have washed my feet; how can I soil them? For I have washed myself with [?] and [?].
My brother’s son reached his hand through the opening, for his heart is sharper than a spear. My inward parts trembled because of him.
I rose to open for my brother’s son. My hands dripped myrrh, and my fingers were full of myrrh.

On the handle of the bolt, I rose to open for my brother’s son. My brother’s son had gone away. My soul trembled at his voice. I searched for him but did not find him. I called him, but he did not answer me.
The watchmen who guard the city found me. They struck me and wounded me. Those who guard the wall took my veil from my head.
I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the power and strength of the wilderness: if you find my brother’s son, tell him that I am stricken with love for him.

How is your brother’s son different from other brothers’ sons, you who are beautiful among women? How is your brother’s son different from other brothers’ sons, that you have put us under such an oath—by the sun, by Yaros [?], and by Kemanyos [?]?
My brother is white and ruddy. Ten thousand and ten thousand times ten thousand surround him, one born among thousands.
His head is the finest gold. His locks hang down, black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside a full pool of water. His teeth are washed in milk and sit beside a full pool of water.

His cheeks are like beds of spices that produce fragrant plants. His eyes are like the morning star; his radiance shines brightly. His lips are flowers dripping pure myrrh. My brother’s son smells of fragrant [?]. His clothes are of [?], like the men of Tarshish.
His hands are rounded gold, adorned with stones of Tarshish. His belly is a slab like ivory upon sapphire stone: precious ornaments and inlay that no craftsman’s hand has inlaid.
His legs are marble pillars set on golden bases. His head is like [?], and he is choice as a cedar.
His mouth is sweet, and he is altogether desirable. My nephew is my beloved.
The bride said, “Where has my nephew gone, daughters of Jerusalem?” And [?] said, “Where has your nephew gone, so that we may look for him with you?”
My nephew has gone down into his garden, into the beds of spices, to tend the garden and gather flowers.
Look, you too, who are with me, are like a delight.
Beautiful as Jerusalem, fearsome as an army in formation.
Turn your eyes away from me, for they have made me soar into the air.
Your hair is like a flock of goats appearing on the mountains of Gilead. Your teeth are like shorn flocks coming up from washing, all of them bearing twins, with none among them barren.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread. Your speech is beautiful. Your cheeks are like a pomegranate rind, apart from your silence.
There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and young women without number.
My dove, the perfect one, is unique. Her wings are silver wings, and her sides are greenish gold.
She is her mother’s only one, the chosen one of the woman who bore her. The daughters saw her and called her blessed; queens and concubines praised her.
Who is this who looks forth like the dawn, beautiful as the moon and bright as the sun? Her movements are mysterious, terrifying like a battle array.
My nephew went down into the walnut garden, into the planting beside the stream, where the [?] bore fruit, to see whether the vine had blossomed and whether the pomegranate had borne fruit.
There I will give you my breasts. My soul did not know; it made me the chariots of Amminadab.
He said to her, “Return, return, Shulammite. Return, so that we may see peace in you.”
What do you see in the woman who gives peace, who dances from afar like a company of people?
How very beautiful is your walk in sandals, daughter of Amminadab! The curves of your thighs resemble a necklace, the work of a craftsman’s hands.
Your navel is like a polished bowl that never lacks mixed wine. Your belly is a heap of wheat fenced around with flowers.
Your two breasts are like two young twin gazelles, flowing with the milk of the Spirit.
Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like a reservoir full of water in Heshbon, at the gates of the daughter of multitudes.
Queens desire your beauty, and nations walk by your radiance. Your nose resembles the tower of Lebanon that looks toward Damascus.
The hair upon you is like Carmel, and the braids of your hair are like purple cloth.
Solomon’s golden tower, whose foundation is a gemstone of [?].
The king has bound the runner. How very lovely and how very beautiful you are!
I love your delights. Your stature resembles a palm tree, and your breasts are like clusters of dates.
I said, “I will climb the palm tree and take hold of its top.” Its height reaches far into the heavens.
May your breasts be like a cluster of grapes, and your mouth like good wine.
As my nephew goes, and as it suits my lips and my tongue. Hyssop and basil and fragrant plants surround the floor of my house. His mouth was sweet to me, like roses and pomegranates and [?].
I belong to my brother’s son, and he turns toward me.

Come, my brother’s son, let us go out into the field. Let us spend the night in the villages, and let us go early to the vineyards. Let us see whether the vine has blossomed, whether the [?] has blossomed, and whether the pomegranate has borne fruit.
His mouth is fragrant to me with [?] and scarlet cloth. There I will give you my breasts, and desire will be separated from others.
The mandrakes have given their fragrance. In our gardens is every kind of produce, new and old. My brother’s son, I have kept it for you.
Who will give you as a son, my brother, nursing at your mother’s breasts? Finding you outside, I would kiss you, and they would not despise me.
I will take you and bring you into my mother’s house, into the chambers of the woman who nursed me. I will give you my spiced wine to drink, and the drink of my pomegranates.
His right arm embraces me, and his left is beneath my head.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the power and strength of the wilderness: when he rose and raised all the dead, [?] love until he wished.

Who is this who comes forth like the dawn, white and radiant, leaning on her brother’s son? I raised you from beside the apple tree. As for the apple tree, which in Hebrew is [?], those anointed with the blood of the [?] of Gilead.
There your mother was in labor with you, and there your mother, the woman who bore you, was in labor with you. The sons of Issachar mock you.
Set me like a signet ring upon your heart, and like a bracelet upon your arm, for love is strong as death. Gold and [?] cannot be its price, and it is fierce as Sheol.
Jealousy devours the hearts of many in wrath, for grace is not found in jealousy. Its wings are wings of fire, a flame.
Much water cannot extinguish love, nor can rivers sweep it away. If a man gave all his possessions for love, they would certainly not despise him.
Our sister is little, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister on the day when people speak about her?
If she is a wall, let us build a silver canopy upon her. If she is a gateway, let us make her a cedar door. A red tower that [?] Solomon in Hebron.
I am a wall, and my breasts are like a tower. I am the one who finds peace in his eyes.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He gave his vineyard to those who guarded its fruit. Each man is to give its fruit in its season.
My vineyard is mine, before me. While he dwells in the garden, others have seen him. Those gathered and hated dwell in peace, and others have seen them.
And while they graze in her midst, and while others walk in the garden.
Let me hear your voice. Flee, you, the Son, my brother, and be like a gazelle and like a young stag on the mountains of incense.
